Problem: Given the function f(x) = (x^2 - 2x)sin(x - 1) + x + 1, calculate the sum of its maximum value M and minimum value m on the interval [-1, 3]. Express your answer as a single number.

<reflection>
f is continuous on [-1, 3], so its extrema on this closed interval occur at critical points or endpoints. f(-1) = -3 sin(2) ≈ -2.7279. f(3) = 3 sin(2) + 4 ≈ 5.7279. f'(x) = (2x - 2) sin(x - 1) + (x^2 - 2x) cos(x - 1) + 1. Critical points satisfy (2x - 2) sin(x - 1) + (x^2 - 2x) cos(x - 1) = -1. f(0) = 1.
This conclusion is not justified because only the endpoints and x=0 have been evaluated; the actual critical points have not been found or checked, so the global maximum and minimum on [-1,3] cannot be determined from these sampled values.
Use the substitution u = x - 1 to rewrite f as 2 plus an odd function on the symmetric interval [-2,2], then deduce M + m directly.
</reflection>
